propositions: Core performs exactly five push-first retry cycles followed by one conditional terminal push; an earlier successful push exits without the terminal push, and only a clean merge from the fifth rejection triggers the terminal sixth push.

Strict delivery mode (opt-in via strict=True keyword argument) raises catchable PushDeliveryError with stable reasons and git detail; best-effort mode (strict=False default) preserves existing warning-and-return behavior for all pre-existing callers.

The private Python module adapter (python -m rebar._store.push push --tracker [--strict]) translates PushDeliveryError to stderr output and nonzero exit, serving as the sole process boundary that owns stream writes and exit codes.

All legacy callers (event append, batch append, NDJSON import, transition close, delete paths, compact paths, claim) either omit strict or explicitly pass strict=False and retain their original push behavior and return disposition.
Strict failure writes no ticket event, emits no BRIDGE_ALERT, and leaves HEAD and working tree unchanged; policy declines are distinct from transport failures via separate stable reason codes.
